A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Unison work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables throughout. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although both reference supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Tables 2–3, and a user study in Figure 9.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and reports a revised user study with additional Gemini scores in Table 4.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, Bi-ACA, SCG, training losses and progressive cross-modal forcing remain unchanged. The added attention-window and lip-filtering descriptions provide technical detail without establishing that the underlying method was revised.

E1.justification: The training corpora and T2AV, TI2AV, audio-to-video and video-to-audio task coverage are retained. Increasing the user-study sample count does not establish a new domain, population or test scenario.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Table 1 and the qualitative comparisons are unchanged. Both user studies compare Unison with UniAVGen, MOVA and LTX-2; the additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The user study changes from 10 samples with 25 participants to 40 samples with 25 participants, described as 1,000 mean-rank votes. V2 also adds Gemini evaluation of motion–speech–sound-effect coherence. The main benchmark protocol and reported training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same component and training-schedule ablations. Figures 6–8 retain the beach and piano examples and the layer-, timestep- and instance-wise gate analyses. HGHS becoming SGHS is a terminology correction.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The user study continues to report average ranks; the increased sample count and explicit vote total concern evaluation design rather than a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–8 retain their results. User-study scores are replaced under the larger sample count: motion–audio alignment changes from Unison 1.86 versus LTX-2 1.98 in v1 Figure 9 to 1.92 versus 1.89 in v2 Table 4, reversing their ranking because lower is better. New Gemini scores favor Unison at 1.68. These are revised study outcomes, not same-setting model performance changes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, including the flow-matching objectives, gating formulation, direction indicator and loss weighting, are retained. No new mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about acoustic harmonization, bidirectional cross-modal forcing, synchronization and state-of-the-art performance. The revised study does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly explains word-level lip synchronization through local attention, face-based filtering of misaligned speech, and cross-modal training dependence. Existing ablation and gate-behavior interpretations remain unchanged, and no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: V2 specifies a three-frame cross-attention window, stride one and retention of the middle-frame representation. It also describes face detection and bounding-box-based SyncNet filtering of unsynchronized speech and off-screen voice-overs. These are newly disclosed details; hardware, training hyperparameters, inference settings and the promised future code/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Zipformer, Out of Time for SyncNet, InteractiveAvatar and several introductory citations. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing audio-video generation and diffusion-forcing approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds the synchronization-details paragraph, revises the user-study description, corrects HGHS to SGHS and replaces the placeholder running title. It also supplies affiliations and acknowledgements and numbers the conclusion. Most prose and section ordering are retained.

P2.justification: V1's user-study bar chart, Figure 9, is replaced by Table 4 with explicit metric directions and an additional Gemini column. Existing figures and tables are repositioned as text reflows, while their principal designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves methodological transparency through concrete attention and filtering specifications and makes the expanded user study easier to inspect. These benefits are tempered by a reporting error: the text still claims the best motion–audio alignment, although Table 4 favors LTX-2 over Unison, 1.89 versus 1.92. Gemini scoring is also insufficiently specified. The gains are therefore limited, with the core method and benchmark evidence unchanged.
